about.title: San Diego Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Eighty-seven people died on San Diego's streets and freeways in 2025, according to the most recent final collision records for the city. Behind each of those counts is a household somewhere in San Diego County trying to figure out what comes next: bills still arriving, a paycheck gone, an empty chair at dinner. Many of those collisions occurred along I-5, I-805, El Cajon Boulevard and University Avenue, the corridors that carry the heaviest traffic through the city, and reported crashes here tend to cluster on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. A California wrongful death claim is a civil case, separate from anything the district attorney may pursue. It exists so a family can recover funeral and burial costs, the financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We listen first, then connect you with an independent San Diego attorney who handles these claims on contingency, meaning nothing is owed unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: What a San Diego Wrongful Death Attorney Brings to Your Family

items.title: Clarity on Who Can File
items.desc: California limits standing: a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children come first, followed by certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can explain where your family fits before anyone files paperwork in San Diego County.

items.title: Protection of the Filing Deadline
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims in California must be brought within two years of the date of death, and the window is considerably shorter when a city, county or state agency is involved. Early guidance keeps those dates from slipping by during a hard season.

items.title: A Full Accounting of What Was Lost
items.desc: Recoverable losses reach beyond funeral and burial expenses to include lost financial support and the loss of love, companionship and guidance. An independent attorney works to document each of these, not just the receipts.

items.question: My family member was killed on I-5 in San Diego and the other driver may face criminal charges. Do we still have a civil claim?
items.answer: Yes. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and moves separately from any criminal case the San Diego County District Attorney may bring. The criminal case is about punishment; the civil claim is about your family's losses. One does not have to finish before the other begins, and an outcome in one does not decide the other.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Generally two years from the date of death. If a government entity is a potential defendant, such as a city vehicle or a public agency responsible for a roadway, a formal claim must usually be filed within a much shorter period first. Because that distinction matters so much, it is worth speaking with an attorney sooner rather than later.

items.question: What can a family actually recover, and what does it cost to find out?
items.answer: California allows recovery of funeral and burial costs, the financial support the person would have contributed, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. Every family's circumstances differ, so no one can tell you a number in advance. LawProactive's connection service is free, and the attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.
